review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

7:1.sourceText: ταύτας οὖν ἔχοντες τὰς ἐπαγγελίας, ἀγαπητοί, καθαρίσωμεν ἑαυτοὺς ἀπὸ παντὸς μολυσμοῦ σαρκὸς καὶ πνεύματος, ἐπιτελοῦντες ἁγιωσύνην ἐν φόβῳ Θεοῦ.
7:1.targetText: Therefore, beloved, since we have these promises, let us cleanse ourselves from everything that defiles body and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.

groups.note: The participle ἔχοντες ("having") is rendered since … have.
The noun μολυσμοῦ ("defilement") is rendered defiles.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject for the participle ἔχοντες.
English introduces the clause made from the noun μολυσμοῦ ("defilement").

7:2.sourceText: Χωρήσατε ἡμᾶς· οὐδένα ἠδικήσαμεν, οὐδένα ἐφθείραμεν, οὐδένα ἐπλεονεκτήσαμεν.
7:2.targetText: Make room for us in your hearts. We have wronged no one, we have corrupted no one, we have exploited no one.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies where room is to be made; the Greek says only "make room for us".

7:3.sourceText: πρὸς κατάκρισιν οὐ λέγω· προείρηκα γὰρ ὅτι ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν ἐστε εἰς τὸ συναποθανεῖν καὶ συνζῆν.
7:3.targetText: I do not say this to condemn you. I have said before that you so occupy our hearts that we live and die together with you.

groups.note: The noun κατάκρισιν ("condemnation") is rendered condemn.
ἐν … ἐστε ("you are in") is rendered you … occupy.
εἰς τό with the infinitive is rendered so … that.
Same verb, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for say.
English supplies an object for condemn.
English supplies a subject for the infinitives.
English supplies the object of with; the Greek verbs ("die with", "live with") name no one.

7:4.sourceText: πολλή μοι παρρησία πρὸς ὑμᾶς, πολλή μοι καύχησις ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν· πεπλήρωμαι τῇ παρακλήσει, ὑπερπερισσεύομαι τῇ χαρᾷ ἐπὶ πάσῃ τῇ θλίψει ἡμῶν.
7:4.targetText: Great is my confidence in you; great is my pride in you; I am filled with encouragement; in all our troubles my joy overflows.

groups.note: ὑπερπερισσεύομαι ("I overflow") is recast with joy as the subject.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula; the Greek clause has no verb.
English supplies a copula; the Greek clause has no verb.

7:5.sourceText: Καὶ γὰρ ἐλθόντων ἡμῶν εἰς Μακεδονίαν οὐδεμίαν ἔσχηκεν ἄνεσιν ἡ σὰρξ ἡμῶν, ἀλλ’ ἐν παντὶ θλιβόμενοι· ἔξωθεν μάχαι, ἔσωθεν φόβοι.
7:5.targetText: For when we arrived in Macedonia, our bodies had no rest, but we were pressed from every direction—conflicts on the outside, fears within.

groups.note: καὶ γάρ ("for indeed") is rendered For.
The genitive absolute ἐλθόντων ἡμῶν ("we having come") is rendered when we arrived.
ἐν παντί ("in every way") is rendered from every direction.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject for the participle θλιβόμενοι ("being pressed").

7:6.sourceText: ἀλλ’ ὁ παρακαλῶν τοὺς ταπεινοὺς παρεκάλεσεν ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεὸς ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ Τίτου·
7:6.targetText: But God, who comforts the downcast, comforted us by the arrival of Titus,

groups.note: The article with the participle παρακαλῶν ("comforting") is rendered who comforts.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:7.sourceText: οὐ μόνον δὲ ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ αὐτοῦ, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν τῇ παρακλήσει ᾗ παρεκλήθη ἐφ’ ὑμῖν, ἀναγγέλλων ἡμῖν τὴν ὑμῶν ἐπιπόθησιν, τὸν ὑμῶν ὀδυρμόν, τὸν ὑμῶν ζῆλον ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ, ὥστε με μᾶλλον χαρῆναι.
7:7.targetText: and not only by his arrival, but also by the comfort he had received from you. He told us about your longing, your mourning, and your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced all the more.

groups.note: παρεκλήθη ("he was comforted") is rendered with the comfort he had received.
The participle ἀναγγέλλων ("reporting") is rendered told … about.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the relative ᾗ ("with which") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject for the participle ἀναγγέλλων and starts a new sentence.
English joins the last item of the list with and; the Greek has no καί here.

7:8.sourceText: ὅτι εἰ καὶ ἐλύπησα ὑμᾶς ἐν τῇ ἐπιστολῇ, οὐ μεταμέλομαι· εἰ καὶ μετεμελόμην, βλέπω ὅτι ἡ ἐπιστολὴ ἐκείνη εἰ καὶ πρὸς ὥραν ἐλύπησεν ὑμᾶς,
7:8.targetText: Even if I caused you sorrow by my letter, I do not regret it. Although I did regret it, I now see that my letter caused you sorrow, but only for a short time.

groups.note: ἐλύπησα ("I grieved") is rendered I caused … sorrow.
The article τῇ is used as a possessive and rendered my.
εἰ καί ("even if") is rendered Although.
The article ἡ is used as a possessive and rendered my.
εἰ καί ("even if") before "for an hour" is rendered but only.
ὥραν ("hour") is rendered a short time.
ἐλύπησεν ("it grieved") is rendered caused … sorrow.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective ὅτι ("for") untranslated.
BSB leaves the demonstrative ἐκείνη ("that") untranslated and says my letter.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for regret.
English supplies an object for regret.
English adds a time word; N1904 has only βλέπω ("I see") here, though BSB's Greek text has an extra word in this verse.

7:9.sourceText: νῦν χαίρω, οὐχ ὅτι ἐλυπήθητε, ἀλλ’ ὅτι ἐλυπήθητε εἰς μετάνοιαν· ἐλυπήθητε γὰρ κατὰ Θεόν, ἵνα ἐν μηδενὶ ζημιωθῆτε ἐξ ἡμῶν.
7:9.targetText: And now I rejoice, not because you were made sorrowful, but because your sorrow led you to repentance. For you felt the sorrow that God had intended, and so were not harmed in any way by us.

groups.note: ἐλυπήθητε ("you were grieved") is rendered your sorrow.
εἰς ("into") is rendered led … to.
ἐλυπήθητε ("you were grieved") is rendered you felt the sorrow.
κατὰ Θεόν ("according to God") is recast as God had intended.
μηδενί ("in nothing") is rendered not … in any way.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a connective; the Greek has none here.
English supplies an object for led.
English supplies a relative frame for κατὰ Θεόν ("according to God").

7:10.sourceText: ἡ γὰρ κατὰ Θεὸν λύπη μετάνοιαν εἰς σωτηρίαν ἀμεταμέλητον ἐργάζεται· ἡ δὲ τοῦ κόσμου λύπη θάνατον κατεργάζεται.
7:10.targetText: Godly sorrow brings repentance that leads to salvation without regret, but worldly sorrow brings death.

groups.note: κατὰ Θεόν ("according to God") is rendered Godly.
εἰς ("into") is rendered leads to.
The genitive κόσμου ("of the world") is rendered worldly.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a relative frame for the phrase εἰς σωτηρίαν ("to salvation").

7:11.sourceText: ἰδοὺ γὰρ αὐτὸ τοῦτο τὸ κατὰ Θεὸν λυπηθῆναι πόσην κατειργάσατο ὑμῖν σπουδήν, ἀλλὰ ἀπολογίαν, ἀλλὰ ἀγανάκτησιν, ἀλλὰ φόβον, ἀλλὰ ἐπιπόθησιν, ἀλλὰ ζῆλον, ἀλλὰ ἐκδίκησιν. ἐν παντὶ συνεστήσατε ἑαυτοὺς ἁγνοὺς εἶναι τῷ πράγματι.
7:11.targetText: Consider what this godly sorrow has produced in you: what earnestness, what eagerness to clear yourselves, what indignation, what alarm, what longing, what zeal, what vindication! In every way you have proved yourselves to be innocent in this matter.

groups.note: ἰδού ("behold") is rendered Consider.
The articular infinitive τὸ λυπηθῆναι ("being grieved") is rendered sorrow.
κατὰ Θεόν ("according to God") is rendered godly.
πόσην ("how much") is rendered what for the thing produced, and BSB repeats it before each item of the list.
ἀπολογίαν ("defense") is rendered eagerness to clear yourselves.
The article τῷ is rendered this, referring back to the matter of the letter.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.
BSB leaves the intensive αὐτό ("very") untranslated.
BSB leaves the ascensive ἀλλά ("indeed, yes") untranslated and joins the list with commas.

7:12.sourceText: ἄρα εἰ καὶ ἔγραψα ὑμῖν, οὐχ ἕνεκεν τοῦ ἀδικήσαντος οὐδὲ ἕνεκεν τοῦ ἀδικηθέντος, ἀλλ’ ἕνεκεν τοῦ φανερωθῆναι τὴν σπουδὴν ὑμῶν τὴν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ.
7:12.targetText: So even though I wrote to you, it was not on account of the one who did wrong or the one who was harmed, but rather that your earnestness on our behalf would be made clear to you in the sight of God.

groups.note: The article with the participle ἀδικήσαντος ("having done wrong") is rendered the one who did wrong.
The article with the participle ἀδικηθέντος ("having been wronged") is rendered the one who was harmed.
ἕνεκεν ("for the sake of") with the infinitive is rendered that.
The articular infinitive τοῦ φανερωθῆναι ("to be made clear") is rendered would be made clear.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not repeat on account of before the second participle.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject and copula; the Greek phrase has no verb.

7:13.sourceText: διὰ τοῦτο παρακεκλήμεθα. Ἐπὶ δὲ τῇ παρακλήσει ἡμῶν περισσοτέρως μᾶλλον ἐχάρημεν ἐπὶ τῇ χαρᾷ Τίτου, ὅτι ἀναπέπαυται τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ πάντων ὑμῶν·
7:13.targetText: On account of this, we are encouraged.  In addition to our own encouragement, we were even more delighted by the joy of Titus. For his spirit has been refreshed by all of you.

groups.note: περισσοτέρως μᾶλλον ("much more still") is rendered even more.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds emphasis; the Greek has only ἡμῶν ("our").

7:14.sourceText: ὅτι εἴ τι αὐτῷ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν κεκαύχημαι, οὐ κατῃσχύνθην, ἀλλ’ ὡς πάντα ἐν ἀληθείᾳ ἐλαλήσαμεν ὑμῖν, οὕτως καὶ ἡ καύχησις ἡμῶν ἐπὶ Τίτου ἀλήθεια ἐγενήθη.
7:14.targetText: Indeed, I was not embarrassed by anything I had boasted to him about you. But just as everything we said to you was true, so our boasting to Titus has proved to be true as well.

groups.note: The connective ὅτι ("for") is rendered Indeed.
εἴ τι ("if … anything") is rendered anything.
ἐν ἀληθείᾳ ("in truth") is rendered true.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies by to join what was boasted to embarrassed.
English supplies a copula; BSB recasts "we spoke everything in truth" as everything we said was true.

7:15.sourceText: καὶ τὰ σπλάγχνα αὐτοῦ περισσοτέρως εἰς ὑμᾶς ἐστιν ἀναμιμνῃσκομένου τὴν πάντων ὑμῶν ὑπακοήν, ὡς μετὰ φόβου καὶ τρόμου ἐδέξασθε αὐτόν.
7:15.targetText: And his affection for you is even greater when he remembers that you were all obedient as you welcomed him with fear and trembling.

groups.note: The participle ἀναμιμνῃσκομένου ("remembering") is rendered when he remembers.
The noun ὑπακοήν ("obedience") is rendered obedient.
ὡς ("how") introduces the welcome and is rendered as.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject for the participle ἀναμιμνῃσκομένου.
English adds that, recasting the noun phrase "the obedience of you all" as a clause.
English supplies a copula for the recast clause.

7:16.sourceText: χαίρω ὅτι ἐν παντὶ θαρρῶ ἐν ὑμῖν.
7:16.targetText: I rejoice that I can have complete confidence in you.

groups.note: ἐν παντί ("in everything") is rendered complete.
